name: One Last Wish
label: Dischord
lede: One Last Wish played six shows in four months, cut twelve songs at Inner Ear, and then waited 13 years for a release, because Dischord didn't want to be the label of dead bands.

eras.title: The house on Garfield Street
eras.text: Revolution Summer changed how D.C. punk sounded, and group houses became its living rooms. In 1985 the Garfield Street house in the Cathedral neighborhood filled up with Rites of Spring's Brendan Canty and Guy Picciotto and Embrace's Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson. By early 1986 both bands were finished, a dozen or so shows apiece.

years.h: Two bands, one roof on Garfield Street
years.p: Canty and Picciotto of [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] share the house near the National Cathedral with Hampton and [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] of [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]].
years.xp: Dischord calls the group house a centerpiece of the D.C. underground for years to come. The band that came out of it had no need for a rehearsal space hunt: the members lived there.

years.h: Embrace play the 9:30 Club one last time
years.p: The bill is [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] and Embrace, and Rites of Spring has already split. Canty, Picciotto and Hampton are all free at once.

years.h: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986
yt: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986

eras.title: Four months, six shows
eras.text: Hampton came up through SOA, Faith and Embrace, and joined three-quarters of Rites of Spring. Dischord says One Last Wish was even more short-lived than those bands: six shows in four months, and one studio session.

years.cap: The four members of One Last Wish, Washington, 1986
years.h: Hampton plus three-quarters of Rites of Spring
years.p: Picciotto sings and plays guitar, [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] takes bass, Canty drums, and Hampton plays guitar and sings. Bassist Mike Fellows is the one Rites of Spring member missing.
years.xp: Dischord puts the start right after Rites of Spring and Embrace split in early 1986; Wikipedia dates the formation to May 1986. Either way, it was roommates and old friends. Janney had played guitar beside Hampton in [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]], and he switched to bass for this band.

yt: Full set, Chevy Chase Community Center, Sept. 26, 1986
years.h: Summer benefit shows, six in all
years.p: Wikipedia has the band playing out from August, mostly D.C. benefits. Dischord counts six shows total.
years.xp: The full set from the Chevy Chase Community Center on September 26, 1986 survives on video, posted by Sohrab Habibion.

eras.title: Shelved, then one song gets out
eras.text: The band dissolved, its members kept playing together in Happy Go Licky and Fugazi, and the Inner Ear tape stayed in a drawer. Dischord didn't want more posthumous releases.

years.h: One Last Wish end in January
years.p: Wikipedia and Punktastic date the split to January 1987. Dischord gives no month, only that the November 1986 Inner Ear session was the band's last activity.

years.h: Three of them regroup as Happy Go Licky, then Fugazi
years.p: Picciotto, Janney and Canty team up with Mike Fellows as [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]]. Canty is drumming for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] by its first show that September, and Picciotto is soon singing with them too.

years.h: Burning in the Undertow turns up on State of the Union
years.p: One song from the 1986 Inner Ear session lands on Dischord's benefit compilation, and Dischord says it only raised interest in the rest of the tape.

eras.title: Named for the only year it lived
eras.text: Ten years after the compilation track, the whole session came out as 1986, titled for the year the band existed. Its reputation has only grown since.

years.p: One Last Wish recorded twelve songs at Inner Ear in November 1986, and Dischord held them back. They finally came out as Dischord No. 118, co-released with Picciotto's Peterbilt label.
years.xp:
[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineered. The session covers the whole songbook, including Hide, Break to Broken, My Better Half, Loss Like a Seed, Three Unkind Silences and Home Is the Place.

Wikipedia and Punktastic both say Dischord didn't want to be viewed as a label of defunct bands, and One Last Wish already was one. After Burning in the Undertow in 1989, the rest waited a decade.

years.h: One Last Wish on the 20 Years of Dischord box
years.p: The anniversary set puts the band next to Rites of Spring and Embrace, the two bands it came out of.

years.h: Vulture puts My Better Half at No. 81
years.p: The song makes Vulture's list of the 100 greatest emo songs, from a band that played six shows.

sources.title: Punktastic: One Last Wish, investigating the short-lived DC emotive hardcore act
